lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: The résumé leaves a 10-month gap between the B.S. and the first listed work role unexplained.
items.because: No study or work is listed between June 2022 and May 2023.

items.says: Education appears before the most relevant professional experience.
items.because: This delays the work history and may make the strongest qualifications less visible.

items.says: The later job title reads as a step back from Junior Software Engineer to Machine Learning Engineering Intern.
The 35% diagnostic-accuracy improvement does not identify its measure or comparison point.
items.because: Without the evaluation measure and baseline, the gain is difficult to assess and defend.

items.says: The routing constraints come before the quantified reduction in reviewer disagreement.
The GRPO method description comes before both quantified results.
The evaluation-harness description comes before the release-safety result.
Assistant-only loss masking does not train the model to reproduce tool outputs faithfully.
items.because: It excludes tool-output tokens from the training loss, so they receive no direct training signal.

items.says: The assistant-only loss-masking method is repeated in a method-only bullet with no distinct result.
items.because: The first bullet already names the method, making one achievement look like two.

items.says: The feature-extraction or modeling approach behind the triage system is unspecified.
The backlog reduction is buried after the system and signal details.
Switching from FP32 to BF16 alone does not establish a 4× total GPU-memory reduction, and no measured memory values or baseline are given.
items.because: Total fine-tuning memory includes activations, gradients, and optimizer state, and the memory measure is unclear.

items.says: The repeated “by” makes the result and method phrase awkward to scan.
The load-test description uses present tense for work in a past role.
The bullet shifts from past to present tense and opens with a duty rather than the specific work performed.
items.because: “Maintained” describes past work while “adds” reads as ongoing, and the broad duty delays the contribution.

items.says: The three-day release-cycle duration has no before-and-after comparison.
items.because: Without the prior duration, the size of the improvement is unclear.

items.says: The automated regression checks are not identified.
The service-migration result is not the opening point of the bullet.
The adoption claim names neither the practices adopted nor a specific result and does not connect clearly to the entry’s technical results.
items.because: The practices and downstream changes are unspecified, so the broad claim reads as disconnected from the other bullets.

items.says: The 100× comparison does not say what grew.
The concurrency changes do not by themselves establish that tool results were no longer lost.
items.because: Gating cache writes does not ensure results reach fan-in; delivery, aggregation, worker-failure, or shared-state issues could still lose them.

items.says: The 50-way fan-out condition gives no measure or verification that deadlocks and lost results were eliminated.
items.because: The scale is clear, but the reliability improvement and how it was confirmed are not.

items.says: The concrete concurrency result is not the opening bullet.
The failure condition is phrased ambiguously.
The metric integration says what was added but not what it enabled or improved.
items.because: Without a change in evaluation coverage or use, its impact is not apparent.

items.says: The 0.89 Kendall correlation does not identify the two quantities being correlated.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the coefficient measures.

items.says: The quantified evaluator result is not the opening bullet.
The result bullet combines a past-tense action with a present-tense clause.
The backlog reduction and sensor-triage achievement appear in both this project and the Mobility Systems Company experience.
items.because: The matching reductions and signal counts may look like the same achievement credited twice.

items.says: The triage method uses team-specific terms that may not explain how the backlog was reduced.
The evaluation-framework entry ends with a sensor-triage claim that appears unrelated to its first two bullets.
items.because: The shift from research-agent evaluation to sensor triage makes the project’s scope harder to understand.
